- TeCH: Text-guided Reconstruction of Lifelike Clothed Humans (Yangyi Huang, Hongwei Yi, Yuliang Xiu, Tingting Liao et al., 2023-08-16) http://arxiv.org/abs/2308.08545v2
  Despite recent research advancements in reconstructing clothed humans from a single image, accurately restoring the "unseen regions" with high-level details remains an unsolved challenge that lacks attention. Existing methods often generate overly smooth back-side surfaces with a blurry texture. But how to effectively capture all visual attributes of an individual from a single image, which are sufficient to reconstruct unseen areas (e.g., the back view)? Motivated by the power of foundation models, TeCH reconstructs the 3D human by leveraging 1) descriptive text prompts (e.g., garments, colors, hairstyles) which are automatically generated via a garment parsing model and Visual Question Answering (VQA), 2) a personalized fine-tuned Text-to-Image diffusion model (T2I) which learns the "indescribable" appearance. To represent high-resolution 3D clothed humans at an affordable cost, we propose a hybrid 3D representation based on DMTet, which consists of an explicit body shape grid and an implicit distance field. Guided by the descriptive prompts + personalized T2I diffusion model, the geometry and texture of the 3D humans are optimized through multi-view Score Distillation Sampling (SDS) and reconstruction losses based on the original observation. TeCH produces high-fidelity 3D clothed humans with consistent & delicate texture, and detailed full-body geometry. Quantitative and qualitative experiments demonstrate that TeCH outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in terms of reconstruction accuracy and rendering quality. The code will be publicly available for research purposes at https://huangyangyi.github.io/TeCH
- Pricing Options on Defaultable Stocks (Erhan Bayraktar, 2007-07-03) http://arxiv.org/abs/0707.0336v2
  In this note, we develop stock option price approximations for a model which takes both the risk o default and the stochastic volatility into account. We also let the intensity of defaults be influenced by the volatility. We show that it might be possible to infer the risk neutral default intensity from the stock option prices. Our option price approximation has a rich implied volatility surface structure and fits the data implied volatility well. Our calibration exercise shows that an effective hazard rate from bonds issued by a company can be used to explain the implied volatility skew of the implied volatility of the option prices issued by the same company.
- Effect of Franchised Business models on Fast Food Company Stock Prices in Recession and Recovery with Weibull Analysis (Sandip Dutta, Vignesh Prabhu, 2019-12-30) http://arxiv.org/abs/1912.12940v1
  At the initial stages of this research, the assumption was that the franchised businesses perhaps should not be affected much by recession as there are multiple cash pools available inherent to the franchised business model. However, after analyzing the available data, it indicated otherwise, the stock price performance as discussed indicates a different pattern. The stock price data is analyzed with an unconventional tool, Weibull distribution and observations confirmed the presence of either a reverse trend in franchised business than what is observed for non-franchised or the franchised stock followed large food suppliers. There is a layered ownership and cash flow in a franchised business model. The parent company run by franchiser depends on the performance of child companies run by franchisees. Both parent and child companies are run as independent businesses but only the parent company is listed as a stock ticker in stock exchange. Does this double layer of vertical operation, cash reserve, and cash flow protect them better in recession? The data analyzed in this paper indicates that the recession effect can be more severe; and if it dives with the average market, expect a slower recover

### What are technology stocks? [...] That distinction is important because not every company will convert technology spending into lasting shareholder value. Investors can improve decision-making by aligning any technology exposure with their goals, time horizon, and tolerance for volatility.

FINDINGS:
- Tech stocks have been experiencing a slump in 2026, with the Nasdaq-100 falling over 9% from its early October peak amid concerns about AI infrastructure spending and the controversy surrounding Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. [source: Goldman Sachs Reportedly Sees AI Hyperscalers As ‘Relatively Defensive’ After Tech Selloff — Forecasts 14% S&P 500 Upside | https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/goldman-sachs-reportedly-sees-ai-115231520.html]
- Goldman Sachs strategists see technology stocks, particularly artificial intelligence (AI) hyperscalers, as relatively defensive investments after a recent selloff pushed their valuations below historical levels. [source: Goldman Sachs Reportedly Sees AI Hyperscalers As ‘Relatively Defensive’ After Tech Selloff — Forecasts 14% S&P 500 Upside | https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/goldman-sachs-reportedly-sees-ai-115231520.html]
- The AI trade may be back, for now, after an early fall slumber, with several under-the-radar moves in the AI sector this week that investors may have overlooked amid the outsized focus on the Huang scandals. [source: 3 signs AI stocks may be a great trade again | https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/article/3-signs-ai-stocks-may-be-a-great-trade-again-130410381.html]
- A selective approach remains the clearest message for investors in technology stocks, with a focus on U.S. companies that are likely to hit earnings targets and considering taking profits in small-cap, micro-cap, and speculative equities. [source: Investing in Tech Stocks | U.S. Bank | https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/investing-in-tech-stocks.html]
- The technology sector still offers meaningful long-term opportunity, but success is likely to depend on selectivity, discipline, and a willingness to look past short-term noise. [source: Investing in Tech Stocks | U.S. Bank | https://www.usbank.com/investing/financial-perspectives/market-news/investing-in-tech-stocks.html]
- Investors should be cautious and consider diversifying their portfolios to avoid the concentration risk associated with tech stocks, which represent as much as 40% of the U.S. large-cap equity market. [source: A lot changed in stock market in just a few months. The single biggest risk did not | https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/15/spx-sp500-tech-stocks-invest.html]
- The tech sell-off could be a brief dip that rebounds to new highs, or it could turn into a bear market, and investors should be prepared for either scenario. [source: If the Tech Stock Sell-Off Turns Into a Bear Market, History Says This Investing Strategy Has Never Failed | https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tech-stock-sell-off-turns-042000090.html]
- The best AI stocks to buy in 2026 include Microsoft, Palantir, Snowflake, Salesforce, and CrowdStrike, according to Wall Street's biggest tech bulls. [source: Best AI Stocks to Buy in 2026: 10 Top Picks & How to Invest | The Motley Fool | https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/market-sectors/information-technology/ai-stocks]
- The 5 best-performing AI stocks right now are Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and Amazon, according to NerdWallet. [source: The 5 Best-Performing AI Stocks Right Now - NerdWallet | https://www.nerdwallet.com/investing/learn/ai-stocks-invest-in-artificial-intelligence]
- Growth stocks can be volatile and require a long-term mindset and diversification across several leaders to balance growth potential with the risk inherent in investing in a new technology. [source: 10 Best Growth Stocks for 2026 and How to Invest | The Motley Fool | https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/types-of-stocks/growth-stocks]
